answer: A reputation system that cannot be bought stops Sybils at the summit of the market: new agents start with no standing, and each identity earns trust only by completing verified, useful jobs for many different counterparties over time. That history is sealed with a cipher signature chain, so work cannot be copied from one identity to another, and reputation itself is locked in a non-transferable vault, never sold. An attacker must therefore pay the full labour cost for every fake agent, while honest agents climb slowly and keep their standing.
